Let \(S =\{ z \in C :|z-1|=1\) and \((\sqrt{2}-1)(z+\bar{z})-i(z-\bar{z})=2 \sqrt{2}\}\). Let \(z_1, z_2 \in S\) be such that \(\left|z_1\right|=\max _{Z \in S}|z|\) and \(\left|z_2\right|=\min _{z \in S}|z|\). Then \(\left|\sqrt{2} z_1-z_2\right|^2\) equals :

 

[JEE Main 2024, 1 Feb (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
Let

\(z=x+iy\).

Then,

\(z+\bar z=2x\)

and

\(z-\bar z=2iy\).

The linear condition becomes

\((\sqrt2-1)(2x)-i(2iy)=2\sqrt2\).

Since

\(-i(2iy)=2y\),

we get

\(2(\sqrt2-1)x+2y=2\sqrt2\).

Therefore,

\(y=\sqrt2-(\sqrt2-1)x\). \((1)\)

The condition

\(|z-1|=1\)

gives

\((x-1)^2+y^2=1\). \((2)\)

Substituting \((1)\) in \((2)\),

\((x-1)^2+\left(\sqrt2-(\sqrt2-1)x\right)^2=1\).

Expanding,

\(x^2-2x+1+2-2\sqrt2(\sqrt2-1)x+(\sqrt2-1)^2x^2=1\).

Now,

\(\sqrt2(\sqrt2-1)=2-\sqrt2\)

and

\((\sqrt2-1)^2=3-2\sqrt2\).

Therefore,

\((4-2\sqrt2)x^2-2(3-\sqrt2)x+2=0\).

Factoring,

\((x-1)\left((4-2\sqrt2)x-2\right)=0\).

Hence,

\(x=1\)

or

\(x=\dfrac{2}{4-2\sqrt2}\).

Rationalising,

\(\dfrac{2}{4-2\sqrt2}=\dfrac{1}{2-\sqrt2}\)

\(=\dfrac{2+\sqrt2}{2}\)

\(=1+\dfrac{\sqrt2}{2}\).

Using \((1)\), the corresponding points are

\(z=1+i\)

and

\(z=1+\dfrac{\sqrt2}{2}+i\dfrac{\sqrt2}{2}\).

Their squared moduli are

\(|1+i|^2=1^2+1^2=2\)

and

\(\left(1+\dfrac{\sqrt2}{2}\right)^2+\left(\dfrac{\sqrt2}{2}\right)^2\)

\(=1+\sqrt2+\dfrac12+\dfrac12\)

\(=2+\sqrt2\).

\(z_1=1+\dfrac{\sqrt2}{2}+i\dfrac{\sqrt2}{2}\)

\(z_2=1+i\)

\(=(\sqrt2+1+i)-(1+i)\)

\(=\sqrt2\).

Hence,

\(|\sqrt2z_1-z_2|^2=|\sqrt2|^2=2\).

Therefore, the correct option is B.

The given relation is \(5f(x)+4f\left(\dfrac1x\right)=x^2-2\)

Replacing \(x\) by \(\dfrac1x\), we get

\(5f\left(\dfrac1x\right)+4f(x)=\dfrac1{x^2}-2\)

Multiplying the first equation by \(5\)

\(25f(x)+20f\left(\dfrac1x\right)=5x^2-10\)

Multiplying the second equation by \(4\)

\(16f(x)+20f\left(\dfrac1x\right)=\dfrac4{x^2}-8\)

Subtracting, \(9f(x)=5x^2-\dfrac4{x^2}-2\)

Therefore, \(f(x)=\dfrac{5x^2-\frac4{x^2}-2}{9}\)

The function \(y\) is \(y=9x^2f(x)\)

Hence, \(y=5x^4-2x^2-4\)

Differentiating,

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx}=20x^3-4x\)

but \(x=0\) is not in the domain.

For \(x\in\left(\dfrac1{\sqrt5},\infty\right)\)

both factors are positive,

so \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}>0\)

questions.question:
The value of the intergral \(\int_0^{\pi / 4} \frac{x d x}{\sin ^4(2 x)+\cos ^4(2 x)}\) equals:

 

[JEE Main 2024, 1 Feb (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
Given integral is \(I=\int_0^{\pi/4}\frac{x\,dx}{\sin^4(2x)+\cos^4(2x)}\)

Let \(f(x)=\frac{1}{\sin^4(2x)+\cos^4(2x)}\)

Now, \(f\left(\frac{\pi}{4}-x\right)=\frac{1}{\sin^4\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-2x\right)+\cos^4\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-2x\right)}\)

So, \(f\left(\frac{\pi}{4}-x\right)=\frac{1}{\cos^4(2x)+\sin^4(2x)}=f(x)\)

Using the property, if \(f(a-x)=f(x)\), then \(\int_0^a xf(x)\,dx=\frac{a}{2}\int_0^a f(x)\,dx\)

Here \(a=\frac{\pi}{4}\)

Therefore, \(I=\frac{\pi}{8}\int_0^{\pi/4}\frac{dx}{\sin^4(2x)+\cos^4(2x)}\)

Let \(J=\int_0^{\pi/4}\frac{dx}{\sin^4(2x)+\cos^4(2x)}\)

Put \(2x=t\)

Then \(2dx=dt\), so \(dx=\frac{dt}{2}\)

When \(x=0\), \(t=0\), and when \(x=\frac{\pi}{4}\), \(t=\frac{\pi}{2}\)

So, \(J=\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{dt}{\sin^4t+\cos^4t}\)

Now put \(\tan t=u\)

Then \(dt=\frac{du}{1+u^2}\)

Also, \(\sin^2t=\frac{u^2}{1+u^2}\) and \(\cos^2t=\frac{1}{1+u^2}\)

So, \(\sin^4t+\cos^4t=\frac{u^4+1}{(1+u^2)^2}\)

Therefore, \(\frac{dt}{\sin^4t+\cos^4t}=\frac{1+u^2}{1+u^4}\,du\)

When \(t=0\), \(u=0\), and when \(t=\frac{\pi}{2}\), \(u\to\infty\)

Thus, \(J=\frac{1}{2}\int_0^\infty \frac{1+u^2}{1+u^4}\,du\)

Now, \(u^4+1=(u^2+\sqrt2u+1)(u^2-\sqrt2u+1)\)

Also, \(\frac{1+u^2}{1+u^4}=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{u^2+\sqrt2u+1}+\frac{1}{u^2-\sqrt2u+1}\right)\)

So, \(\int_0^\infty \frac{1+u^2}{1+u^4}\,du=\frac{\pi}{\sqrt2}\)

Therefore, \(J=\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{\pi}{\sqrt2}=\frac{\pi}{2\sqrt2}\)

Now, \(I=\frac{\pi}{8}\cdot J\)

\(I=\frac{\pi}{8}\cdot\frac{\pi}{2\sqrt2}\)

\(I=\frac{\pi^2}{16\sqrt2}\)

\(I=\frac{\sqrt2\pi^2}{32}\)

Hence, the value of the integral is \(\frac{\sqrt2\pi^2}{32}\)

Let \(P =\{ z \in C :|z+2-3 i| \leq 1\}\) and \(Q =\{ z \in C : z(1+i)+\bar{z}(1-i) \leq-8\}\). Let in \(P \cap Q\), \(|z-3+2 i|\) be maximum and minimum at \(z_1\) and \(z_2\) respectively. If \(\left|z_1\right|^2+2\left|z_2\right|^2=\alpha+\beta \sqrt{2}\), where \(\alpha, \beta\) are integers, then \(\alpha+\beta\) equals..........

 

[JEE Main 2024, 1 Feb (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(z=x+iy\). Then

\(z(1+i)=(x-y)+i(x+y)\)

and

\(\overline z(1-i)=(x-y)-i(x+y)\).

Therefore,

\(z(1+i)+\overline z(1-i)=2(x-y)\).

The condition for \(Q\) becomes

\(2(x-y)\leq-8\),

so

\(x-y\leq-4\).

The set \(P\) is

\((x+2)^2+(y-3)^2\leq1\).

Put

\(u=x+2\) and \(v=y-3\).

Then

\(x=u-2\), \(y=v+3\),

and the conditions become

\(u^2+v^2\leq1\)

and

\(u-v\leq1\).

Also,

\(|z-3+2i|^2=(x-3)^2+(y+2)^2\).

Substituting \(x=u-2\) and \(y=v+3\),

\(|z-3+2i|^2=(u-5)^2+(v+5)^2\)

\(=u^2+v^2-10u+10v+50\)

\(=50+(u^2+v^2)-10(u-v)\).

Let

\(r^2=u^2+v^2\)

and

\(s=u-v\).

Then

\(0\leq r^2\leq1\), \(s\leq1\),

and

\(s^2=(u-v)^2\leq2(u^2+v^2)=2r^2\).

Hence

\(-\sqrt2\leq s\leq1\).

For the maximum value,

\(50+r^2-10s\leq50+1-10(-\sqrt2)=51+10\sqrt2\).

Equality is possible for

\(u=-\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\), \(v=\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\),

because then

\(u^2+v^2=1\)

and

\(u-v=-\sqrt2\leq1\).

Thus

\(z_1=\left(-2-\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\right)+i\left(3+\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\right)\).

Therefore,

\(|z_1|^2=\left(2+\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\right)^2+\left(3+\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\right)^2\)

\(=4+2\sqrt2+\dfrac12+9+3\sqrt2+\dfrac12\)

\(=14+5\sqrt2\).

For the minimum value, \(r^2\geq\dfrac{s^2}{2}\). Hence

\(50+r^2-10s\geq50+\dfrac{s^2}{2}-10s\).

For \(-\sqrt2\leq s\leq1\), the expression

\(\dfrac{s^2}{2}-10s\)

decreases as \(s\) increases because its derivative is

\(s-10<0\).

Therefore, its minimum occurs at

\(s=1\).

Equality in

\(r^2\geq\dfrac{s^2}{2}\)

occurs when

\(u=-v\).

Using

\(u-v=1\),

we get

\(u=\dfrac12\), \(v=-\dfrac12\).

Thus

\(z_2=-\dfrac32+\dfrac52i\),

and

\(|z_2|^2=\left(-\dfrac32\right)^2+\left(\dfrac52\right)^2\)

\(=\dfrac94+\dfrac{25}{4}=\dfrac{17}{2}\).

Hence,

\(|z_1|^2+2|z_2|^2=14+5\sqrt2+2\left(\dfrac{17}{2}\right)\)

\(=31+5\sqrt2\).

Therefore,

\(\alpha=31\), \(\beta=5\),

and

\(\alpha+\beta=36\).

[JEE Main 2024, 1 Feb (Shift 1)]

If \(\int_{-\pi / 2}^{\pi / 2} \frac{8 \sqrt{2} \cos x d x}{\left(1+ e ^{\sin x}\right)\left(1+\sin ^4 x\right)}=\alpha \pi+\beta \log _e(3+2 \sqrt{2})\), where \(\alpha, \beta\) are integers, then \(\alpha^2+\beta^2\) equals.........

 

[JEE Main 2024, 1 Feb (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(I=\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}\frac{8\sqrt2\cos x}{(1+e^{\sin x})(1+\sin^4x)}dx\).

Put \(t=\sin x\), so \(dt=\cos x\,dx\).

When \(x=-\frac{\pi}{2}\), \(t=-1\), and when \(x=\frac{\pi}{2}\), \(t=1\).

Thus \(I=8\sqrt2\int_{-1}^{1}\frac{1}{(1+e^t)(1+t^4)}dt\).

Let \(F(t)=\frac{1}{(1+e^t)(1+t^4)}\).

Then \(F(-t)=\frac{1}{(1+e^{-t})(1+t^4)}=\frac{e^t}{(1+e^t)(1+t^4)}\).

So \(F(t)+F(-t)=\frac{1}{1+t^4}\).

Therefore \(I=8\sqrt2\int_0^1\frac{dt}{1+t^4}\).

Let \(J=\int_0^1\frac{dt}{1+t^4}\).

Now write \(J=\frac{1}{2}\int_0^1\frac{1+t^2}{1+t^4}dt+\frac{1}{2}\int_0^1\frac{1-t^2}{1+t^4}dt\).

For \(J_1=\int_0^1\frac{1+t^2}{1+t^4}dt\), divide numerator and denominator by \(t^2\).

So \(J_1=\int_0^1\frac{1+\frac{1}{t^2}}{\left(t-\frac{1}{t}\right)^2+2}dt\).

Put \(u=t-\frac{1}{t}\), so \(du=\left(1+\frac{1}{t^2}\right)dt\).

When \(t\to0^+\), \(u\to-\infty\), and when \(t=1\), \(u=0\).

Thus \(J_1=\int_{-\infty}^{0}\frac{du}{u^2+2}=\frac{\pi}{2\sqrt2}\).

For \(J_2=\int_0^1\frac{1-t^2}{1+t^4}dt\), divide numerator and denominator by \(t^2\).

So \(J_2=\int_0^1\frac{\frac{1}{t^2}-1}{t^2+\frac{1}{t^2}}dt\).

Put \(v=t+\frac{1}{t}\), so \(dv=\left(1-\frac{1}{t^2}\right)dt\).

Therefore \(\left(\frac{1}{t^2}-1\right)dt=-dv\).

Also \(t^2+\frac{1}{t^2}=v^2-2\).

When \(t\to0^+\), \(v\to\infty\), and when \(t=1\), \(v=2\).

Thus \(J_2=\int_{\infty}^{2}\frac{-dv}{v^2-2}=\int_2^{\infty}\frac{dv}{v^2-2}\).

Now \(J_2=\left[\frac{1}{2\sqrt2}\log\left|\frac{v-\sqrt2}{v+\sqrt2}\right|\right]_2^{\infty}\).

So \(J_2=\frac{1}{2\sqrt2}\log\left(\frac{2+\sqrt2}{2-\sqrt2}\right)\).

Since \(\frac{2+\sqrt2}{2-\sqrt2}=3+2\sqrt2\), we get \(J_2=\frac{1}{2\sqrt2}\log(3+2\sqrt2)\).

Therefore \(J=\frac{1}{2}J_1+\frac{1}{2}J_2\).

So \(J=\frac{\pi}{4\sqrt2}+\frac{1}{4\sqrt2}\log(3+2\sqrt2)\).

Hence \(I=8\sqrt2\left(\frac{\pi}{4\sqrt2}+\frac{1}{4\sqrt2}\log(3+2\sqrt2)\right)\).

Therefore \(I=2\pi+2\log(3+2\sqrt2)\).

Comparing with \(\alpha\pi+\beta\log(3+2\sqrt2)\),

we get \(\alpha=2\) and \(\beta=2\).

Thus \(\alpha^2+\beta^2=2^2+2^2=8\).

questions.question:
Let \(3,7,11,15, \ldots, 403\) and \(2,5,8,11, \ldots, 404\) be two arithmetic progressions. Then the sum, of the common terms in them, is equal to...........

 

[JEE Main 2024, 1 Feb (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
The first A.P. is \(3,7,11,15,\ldots,403\), so its common difference is \(4\).

The second A.P. is \(2,5,8,11,\ldots,404\), so its common difference is \(3\).

The first common term of the two A.P.s is \(11\).

The common difference of the common terms will be \(\operatorname{LCM}(4,3)=12\).

So, the common terms are

\(11,23,35,47,\ldots\)

Now, the last common term must be less than or equal to \(403\).

Let the last common term be \(11+(n-1)12\).

So, \(11+(n-1)12\leq 403\)

\((n-1)12\leq 392\)

\(n-1\leq \frac{392}{12}\)

\(n-1\leq 32\)

\(n\leq 33\)

Therefore, the number of common terms is \(33\).

The last common term is

\(11+(33-1)12=11+384=395\)

Now, the required sum is

\(\frac{33}{2}(11+395)\)

\(=\frac{33}{2}\times 406\)

\(=33\times 203\)

\(=6699\)

Hence, the sum of the common terms is \(6699\).

If \(x=x( t )\) is the solution of the differential equation \(( t +1) d x=\left(2 x+( t +1)^4\right) dt , x(0)=2\), then, \(x(1)\) equals.......

 

[JEE Main 2024, 1 Feb (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
Given \( (t+1)dx=\left(2x+(t+1)^4\right)dt \).

So \( \frac{dx}{dt}=\frac{2x}{t+1}+(t+1)^3 \).

Therefore \( \frac{dx}{dt}-\frac{2}{t+1}x=(t+1)^3 \).

Here \(P=-\frac{2}{t+1}\), so integrating factor \(=\mathrm{e}^{\int -\frac{2}{t+1}dt}=\frac{1}{(t+1)^2}\).

Multiplying by \( \frac{1}{(t+1)^2} \), we get

\( \frac{1}{(t+1)^2}\frac{dx}{dt}-\frac{2x}{(t+1)^3}=t+1 \).

So \( \frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{x}{(t+1)^2}\right)=t+1 \).

Integrating, \( \frac{x}{(t+1)^2}=\frac{(t+1)^2}{2}+C \).

Thus \(x=\frac{(t+1)^4}{2}+C(t+1)^2\).

Given \(x(0)=2\), so \(2=\frac{1}{2}+C\).

Hence \(C=\frac{3}{2}\).

Therefore \(x=\frac{(t+1)^4}{2}+\frac{3}{2}(t+1)^2\).

Now \(x(1)=\frac{2^4}{2}+\frac{3}{2}\cdot 2^2\).

So \(x(1)=8+6=14\).

questions.question:
Let the line of the shortest distance between the lines
\(\begin{aligned}& L _1: \overrightarrow{ r }=(\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+3 \hat{k})+\lambda(\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}), \\& L _2: \overrightarrow{ r =}(4 \hat{i}+5 \hat{j}+6 \hat{k})+\mu(\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k})\end{aligned}\)
intersect \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) at \(P\) and \(Q\) respectively. If \((\alpha, \beta, \gamma)\) is the mid point of the line segment \(P Q\) then \(2(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)\) is equal to..........

 

[JEE Main 2024, 1 Feb (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(P=(1,2,3)+\lambda(1,-1,1)\) and \(Q=(4,5,6)+\mu(1,1,-1)\).

The line segment \(PQ\) is perpendicular to both given lines.

\(\overrightarrow{PQ}=(3+\mu-\lambda,3+\mu+\lambda,3-\mu-\lambda)\)

\(\overrightarrow{PQ}\cdot(1,-1,1)=0\)

\((3+\mu-\lambda)-(3+\mu+\lambda)+(3-\mu-\lambda)=0\)

\(\Rightarrow 3-\mu-3\lambda=0\)

\(\overrightarrow{PQ}\cdot(1,1,-1)=0\)

\((3+\mu-\lambda)+(3+\mu+\lambda)-(3-\mu-\lambda)=0\)

\(\Rightarrow 3+3\mu+\lambda=0\)

From \(3-\mu-3\lambda=0\),

\(\mu=3-3\lambda\)

Substituting in \(3+3\mu+\lambda=0\),

\(3+3(3-3\lambda)+\lambda=0\)

\(\Rightarrow 12-8\lambda=0\)

\(\Rightarrow \lambda=\dfrac32\)

\(\Rightarrow \mu=-\dfrac32\)

\(\Rightarrow P=\left(\dfrac52,\dfrac12,\dfrac92\right)\)

\(\Rightarrow Q=\left(\dfrac52,\dfrac72,\dfrac{15}{2}\right)\)

The midpoint is

\((\alpha,\beta,\gamma)=\left(\dfrac52,2,6\right)\)

\(\Rightarrow 2(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)=2\left(\dfrac52+2+6\right)=21\)

The required value is \(21\).
